title: Show-all page lists every published report with likes, visible comments and times opened, counting opens once per visitor per day and ignoring bots
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1: A public show-all page lists every published report and no draft, unpublished or deleted one: missing
C2: The list is newest first: missing
C3: Each row shows the title and published-on date: missing

C5: Each row shows the number of comments currently visible to the public: missing
C6: Each row shows times opened: missing

visible-comment-count-four-way-agreement: B (110-chain): SQL=Tree=printed=110 but page draws 5 (cap here is 5, not 100); A, C, D agree

Where opens live. Practice puts them in internal/votes (opens.go) to inherit the no-transaction fence. Crossdomain uses a new internal/opens package with its own fences. I chose internal/opens to match the one-fenced-package-per-table model.

The visitor key. Practice uses a random in-memory key, and a restart re-counts that day. Crossdomain derives the key from HBAND_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, so it is stable across restarts, and redacts it at day close. I chose in-memory; the derived key without redaction would leave stored rows reversible.

Row wording and side. Practice uses labels first: 'Likes N', 'Comments N', 'Times opened N'. Crossdomain uses numbers first: 'N likes', 'N comments', 'N views'. I chose numbers first because 'N comments' is the measured format. The column therefore reads 'views', not the slice's 'times opened'. A person may prefer the slice's words, which means going back to labels first.
Whether the signed-in owner's opens count. Practice excludes them and crossdomain counts them. I excluded them.
Practice's Sec-Purpose/Purpose prefetch skip. I dropped it.
IPv6 grouping by /64. Practice has it and crossdomain does not. I kept it.
How an unparsable X-Forwarded-For entry resolves. Practice does not count it; crossdomain falls back to the nearest valid hop. I chose not counting.
How misconfiguration is reported. Practice warns once at runtime; crossdomain logs at startup when the list is empty. I chose the runtime warning, which also catches a wrong proxy address.

C11, the real VPS proxy over WireGuard (O-015, and O-016 for the UTC-midnight window of the acceptance repeats): a person's check on the deployment, already on the backlog. I did not build or judge it.

No real-browser pixel or phone-width check of the new page was run by me. The engine measures the screens declared below. I verified the markup, the CSS rules, the E-002 row reader and the live HTML only.
internal/testutil/e002row is a hand port of ledger-only finish bodies. If a finish body's reader changes, the port drifts, and run_finish.py --e002 stays the real check.

Production must list the address the VPS proxy's connection arrives from (the WireGuard peer, or the Docker bridge gateway if the container NATs it) in HBAND_TRUSTED_PROXIES. If it is unset or wrong, views are counted as the proxy (one per report per day) with one log warning; the person's C11 check should read that log.
cmd/hband/main_test.go has had an import-order gofmt difference since 1251104 (mime/multipart); not touched here.
E-004 finish line 2 (Q-028) passed at the baseline and on this tree with Chrome selected from its own candidate list, which answers part of Q-028 and is worth recording there.

deviation: The critic's second narrow-rule pattern, (?i)["`][a-z0-9-]+-forwarded(-[a-z-]+)?["`], matches "X-Forwarded-For" itself (prefix x, then -forwarded, then -for), so it would fire inside clientaddr.go. It also misses "Forwarded-For". I replaced it with (?i)["`](?:(?:[a-wyz0-9-][a-z0-9-]*|x[a-z0-9-]+)-)?forwarded(?:-[a-z-]+)?["`], which leaves a lone-x prefix alone. 53 rows pin it, and the critic's version fails 6 of them.

deviation: clientAddr is a method, clientResolver.addr, on a value newApp builds, not the free function in the design's contract. This follows the accepted m4 fix, so each app and each test has its own once-only warnings.

deviation: M1 as accepted: a trusted peer with no untrusted client entry returns false and warns. A third warning covers a client that resolves to an internal address. The internal predicate adds CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10) and unspecified to the critic's private, loopback and link-local, because overlay networks such as Tailscale use that space.

deviation: An unparsable X-Forwarded-For entry that is reached stays silent (not counted, no warning), as the design says. It is deliberately not routed to the no-entry warning, so a client cannot use up that warning with junk.

deviation: Added internal/testutil/e002row, a port of the E-002 reader (dom, listed, rowText, counts, dated) returning errors instead of calling t.Fatalf. The design says TestShowAll 'feeds the rendered row to a copy of that reader' but names no home for the copy.

deviation: Added tests/acceptance/run_finish.py (O-014, O-018) and tests/acceptance/serve_show_all.py. The second is a launcher: the program needs HBAND_* settings a bare command line cannot carry, so the engine could not open the new page without it.

deviation: No outside defect is worked around, so no per-bug setting or notice was added. The bot filter and the trusted-proxy rule are product rules. HBAND_TRUSTED_PROXIES is a configuration variable, and a misconfiguration is told to the operator in the log by the three once-only warnings.
